        "contents": "# Tappka\n\nTappka as the app all-in-one web app for Tiimiakatemia Prague.\n\n## Features\n\n- [ ] Authentication\n- [ ] Room booking\n- [ ] Essay Bank\n\n# Links\n\n## Publicly available\n- [Tappka](https://tiimi.cz)\n- [Tappka preview](https://preview.tiimi.cz)\n\n## Locally available when running the project\n- [Tappka locally](http://localhost:3000)\n- [Supabase locally](http://localhost:54323)\n- [Supabase mail locally](http://localhost:54324)\n\n## Other links\n\n- [Blacksmith](https://app.blacksmith.sh/tiimiakatemiapragueit/runs/jobs) - CI/CD for the project\n- [Supabase](https://supabase.com/dashboard/org/zjdqjjekgwwysjkouxpf) - Database for the project\n- [Vercel](https://vercel.com/spirit-of-taps-projects/tappka) - Hosting for the project\n- [Cloudflare DNS](https://dash.cloudflare.com/09d0b565479ef597d4c1bfa2062078b5/tiimi.cz/dns/records) - DNS for the project\n- [Axiom](https://app.axiom.co/spirit-of-tap-9eje) - Logging for the project\n\n# Language\n\nThe project is written in english and will be written in english for better llm compatibility.\nAll czech should be just in localization files.\n\n# Local Development\n\n## Setup\n\n1. Install git if already not installed - https://git-scm.com/install/\n2. Install node.js v24.x with pnpm 10.x if already not installed - https://nodejs.org/en/download/\n3. Install pnpm v10.x if you didn't choose it in the previous step\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm install -g pnpm@10.28.1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Clone the repository \n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ngit clone https://github.com/tappka/tappka.git\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n5. Navigate to the project directory - \n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd tappka\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Running the project after setup\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npnpm install &amp;&amp; pnpm dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe project will be available at [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000)\n\n\n# Supabase\n\nSupabase database is developed locally and synced automatically whenever pushed. See [.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml](.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml) for more details.\nSupabase Auth needs to be configured both on the project itself and in the local development environment.\nMake sure that the project can run without setting up any environment variables, this is so that we can get new T's to start vibecoding without them giving up.",

        "contents": "export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {\n  try {\n    const body = await request.json();\n    const validated = schema.parse(body);\n    \n    // business logic\n    \n    return NextResponse.json({ success: true });\n  } catch (error) {\n    if (error instanceof CustomError) {\n      return NextResponse.json(\n        { error: error.message },\n        { status: error.statusCode }\n      );\n    }\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { error: 'Invalid request' },\n      { status: 400 }\n    );\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Component Template\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// components/Example.tsx\nimport { Suspense } from 'react';\n\ninterface ExampleProps {\n  // props interface\n}\n\nexport function Example({ ...props }: ExampleProps) {\n  return (\n    &lt;Suspense fallback={&lt;div&gt;Loading...&lt;/div&gt;}&gt;\n      {/* component content */}\n    &lt;/Suspense&gt;\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### UI Component Guidelines\n\n- **Always use shadcn/ui** for base UI components\n- **Add new shadcn components** using: &#96;pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add &lt;component&gt;&#96;\n- **Extend shadcn components** rather than creating from scratch\n- **Use Tailwind CSS** for custom styling and layout\n- **Follow shadcn patterns** for component composition\n- **Prefer controlled components** with proper state management\n\n### Test Template\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// __tests__/example.test.ts\nimport { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';\nimport { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';\n\n// Mock external dependencies only\nvi.mock('external-library');\n\ndescribe('Example', () =&gt; {\n  it('should render correctly', () =&gt; {\n    // test implementation\n  });\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Commands\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Development\npnpm dev          # Start development server\npnpm build        # Build for production\npnpm start        # Start production server\n\n# Quality\npnpm typecheck    # TypeScript check\npnpm lint         # ESLint\npnpm test         # Run tests\npnpm test:watch   # Watch mode tests\n\n# Database\npnpm db:generate  # Generate migrations\npnpm db:migrate   # Run migrations\npnpm db:seed      # Seed database\n\n# UI Components\npnpm dlx shadcn@latest add &lt;component&gt;  # Add shadcn/ui component\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./README.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {

          "endPosition": {
            "line": 78,
            "column": 252
          }
        },
        "contents": "Supabase Auth needs to be configured both on the project itself and in the local development environment.\nMake sure that the project can run without setting up any environment variables, this is so that we can get new T's to start vibecoding without them giving up.\n\n# Recommended Tools\n\nIt is very nice to setup mcp with cursor for supabase. Look at [Supabase locally](http://localhost:54323) and go to the top for connection button. It will give you the option.\nThere are cursor rules made for this nextjs project.\n\n# Publishing the project to the public\n\nYou can simply **push to the preview branch** and it will be deployed to the preview environment.\nFor production you will need to make a **pull request to the production branch** and it will be deployed to the production environment. You can approve it yourself, it's just for protection so that you don't accidentally deploy something to production.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "Supabase Auth needs to be configured both on the project itself and in the local development environment.",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "Make sure that the project can run without setting up any environment variables, this is so that we can get new T's to start vibecoding without them giving up.",
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "text": "# Recommended Tools",
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "text": "It is very nice to setup mcp with cursor for supabase. Look at [Supabase locally](http://localhost:54323) and go to the top for connection button. It will give you the option.",
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "There are cursor rules made for this nextjs project.",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "# Publishing the project to the public",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "You can simply **push to the preview branch** and it will be deployed to the preview environment.",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "For production you will need to make a **pull request to the production branch** and it will be deployed to the production environment. You can approve it yourself, it's just for protection so that you don't accidentally deploy something to production.",
            "lineNumber": 79
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.38523876667022705

            "column": 59
          }
        },
        "contents": "// Run supabase status and parse output\nconst output = execSync('pnpm supabase status -o env', { encoding: 'utf-8' });\nconst newEnvVars = {};\n\nfor (const line of output.split('\\n')) {\n  const match = line.match(/^(\\w+)=\"(.+)\"$/);\n  if (match &amp;&amp; keyMapping[match[1]]) {\n    newEnvVars[keyMapping[match[1]]] = match[2];\n  }\n}\n\n// Read existing .env.local if it exists\nconst envLocalPath = path.join(__dirname, '..', '.env.local');\nlet existingEnvVars = {};\n\nif (fs.existsSync(envLocalPath)) {\n  const existingContent = fs.readFileSync(envLocalPath, 'utf-8');\n  existingEnvVars = parseEnvContent(existingContent);\n}\n\n// Merge: update existing vars with new values, keep others unchanged\nconst mergedEnvVars = {\n  ...existingEnvVars,\n  ...newEnvVars,\n};\n\n// Write merged content to .env.local\nconst envContent = formatEnvContent(mergedEnvVars);\nfs.writeFileSync(envLocalPath, envContent + '\\n');\nconsole.log('Environment variables updated in .env.local');",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "[db.migrations]\n# If disabled, migrations will be skipped during a db push or reset.\nenabled = true\n# Specifies an ordered list of schema files that describe your database.\n# Supports glob patterns relative to supabase directory: \"./schemas/*.sql\"\nschema_paths = []\n\n[db.seed]\n# If enabled, seeds the database after migrations during a db reset.\nenabled = true\n# Specifies an ordered list of seed files to load during db reset.\n# Supports glob patterns relative to supabase directory: \"./seeds/*.sql\"\nsql_paths = [\"./seed.sql\"]\n\n[db.network_restrictions]\n# Enable management of network restrictions.\nenabled = false\n# List of IPv4 CIDR blocks allowed to connect to the database.\n# Defaults to allow all IPv4 connections. Set empty array to block all IPs.\nallowed_cidrs = [\"0.0.0.0/0\"]\n# List of IPv6 CIDR blocks allowed to connect to the database.\n# Defaults to allow all IPv6 connections. Set empty array to block all IPs.\nallowed_cidrs_v6 = [\"::/0\"]\n\n[realtime]\nenabled = true\n# Bind realtime via either IPv4 or IPv6. (default: IPv4)\n# ip_version = \"IPv6\"\n# The maximum length in bytes of HTTP request headers. (default: 4096)\n# max_header_length = 4096\n\n[studio]\nenabled = true\n# Port to use for Supabase Studio.\nport = 54323\n# External URL of the API server that frontend connects to.\napi_url = \"http://127.0.0.1\"\n# OpenAI API Key to use for Supabase AI in the Supabase Studio.\nopenai_api_key = \"env(OPENAI_API_KEY)\"\n\n# Email testing server. Emails sent with the local dev setup are not actually sent - rather, they\n# are monitored, and you can view the emails that would have been sent from the web interface.\n[inbucket]\nenabled = true\n# Port to use for the email testing server web interface.\nport = 54324\n# Uncomment to expose additional ports for testing user applications that send emails.\n# smtp_port = 54325\n# pop3_port = 54326\n# admin_email = \"admin@email.com\"\n# sender_name = \"Admin\"\n\n[storage]\nenabled = true\n# The maximum file size allowed (e.g. \"5MB\", \"500KB\").\nfile_size_limit = \"50MiB\"\n\n# Uncomment to configure local storage buckets\n# [storage.buckets.images]\n# public = false\n# file_size_limit = \"50MiB\"",

        "contents": "pnpm db:seed      # Seed database\n\n# UI Components\npnpm dlx shadcn@latest add &lt;component&gt;  # Add shadcn/ui component\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nvi.mock('external-library');\n\ndescribe('Example', () =&gt; {\n  it('should render correctly', () =&gt; {\n    // test implementation\n  });\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Commands\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Development\npnpm dev          # Start development server\npnpm build        # Build for production\npnpm start        # Start production server\n\n# Quality\npnpm typecheck    # TypeScript check\npnpm lint         # ESLint\npnpm test         # Run tests\npnpm test:watch   # Watch mode tests\n\n# Database\npnpm db:generate  # Generate migrations\npnpm db:migrate   # Run migrations\npnpm db:seed      # Seed database\n\n\n- Use type-safe ORMs (Drizzle, Prisma, etc.)\n- Define schemas with proper relationships and constraints\n- Infer types from schema definitions\n- Write repository-style helpers to isolate queries\n- Implement proper migrations\n\n### Data Access Patterns\n\n- Keep database queries in dedicated modules\n- Avoid N+1 queries; use joins and CTEs\n- Implement pagination for list endpoints\n- Use select projections to limit payload size\n\n## Authentication &amp; Authorization\n\n- Implement server-side auth checks\n- Never trust client-side auth flags\n- Use middleware for route protection\n- Store user data securely with proper encryption\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Unit Testing (Vitest)\n\n- **Never mock internal code** - only mock external dependencies\n- Use MSW for API mocking when needed\n- Test utilities, repositories, and business logic\n- Mock external services (APIs, databases, file systems)\n\n### Component Testing (React Testing Library)\n\n- Test interactive components with proper accessibility\n- Ensure loading and error states are covered\n- Test user interactions and state changes\n- Use data-testid sparingly; prefer semantic queries\n\n### Integration Testing\n\n- Test API endpoints with real database connections\n- Use test databases with proper cleanup\n- Test authentication flows end-to-end\n- Mock external services consistently\n\n### Test Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Example test structure",

        "contents": "### Channel Structure Optimization\n- Use one channel per logical scope (&#96;room:123&#96;, not &#96;user:456:room:123&#96;)\n- Shard high-volume topics: &#96;chat:shard:1&#96;, &#96;chat:shard:2&#96;\n- Ensure you have enough connections set in your pool, you can refer to [Realtime Settings](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/settings) and the option &#96;Database connection pool size&#96; to set it.\n\n## Debugging\n\n### Enhanced Logging\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nconst supabase = createClient(url, key, {\n  realtime: {\n    params: { log_level: 'info' }\n  }\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Migration from Postgres Changes\n\n### Step 1: Replace Client Code\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// ❌ Remove postgres_changes\nconst oldChannel = supabase.channel('changes').on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'messages' }, callback)\n\n// ✅ Replace with broadcast\nconst room_id = \"room_id\" // or any other identifier that you use in the trigger function\nconst newChannel = supabase.channel(&#96;messages:${room_id}:changes&#96;, {\n  config: { private: true }\n})\n.on('broadcast', { event: 'INSERT' }, callback)\n.on('broadcast', { event: 'DELETE' }, callback)\n.on('broadcast', { event: 'UPDATE' }, callback)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Add Database Trigger (Only if using broadcast)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE TRIGGER messages_broadcast_trigger\n  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON messages\n  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION notify_table_changes();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: Setup Authorization (Only if using broadcast)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE POLICY \"users_can_receive_broadcasts\" ON realtime.messages\n  FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## LLM Implementation Guidelines\n\n### When Generating Code\n1. **Prefer using &#96;broadcast&#96; over &#96;postgres_changes&#96;** - Never suggest &#96;postgres_changes&#96;\n2.**Include state checking** - Check channel state before subscribing\n3. **Add cleanup logic** - Include unsubscribe in all examples\n4. **Suggest proper naming** - Use consistent topic/event conventions\n5. **Include error handling** - Add reconnection patterns\n6. **Recommend indexing** - When RLS policies are used\n7. **Framework-agnostic** - Adapt patterns to user's framework\n8. **Inform users to prefer the usage of private channels only** - users can refer to [Realtime Settings](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/settings) to enable it.",

          },
          {
            "text": "### When Generating Code",

          },

        },
        "contents": "## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\n\n[auth.email]\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\n\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\n\n- **Profile Linked**: Check &#96;profiles.user_id&#96; matches current auth.user.id\n- **Access Active**: Check &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **User Role**: Read &#96;profiles.role&#96; column (student, team_leader, coach, admin)\n\nThis approach:\n\n- Keeps all business logic in Next.js (single source of truth)\n- Allows real-time updates (e.g., instant access revocation)\n- Admin pre-creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n- Supabase only handles auth + data storage (no custom hooks or functions)\n\n## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP\n\nThe project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:\n\n1. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally\n2. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and profile data\n3. **Testing verification logic**: Query profiles table for auth checks\n\n**Useful MCP commands for development:**\n\n- Seed test data into profiles table for auth testing\n- Inspect auth.users and profiles tables\n- Test profile linking and access revocation queries\n\n## Key Security Features\n\n### Supabase (Data Layer Only)\n\n1. **Database Constraints**:\n\n   - Domain constraint ensures only valid CZU domains in profiles\n   - Unique constraints on work_email, user_id\n\n2. **No RLS or Functions**:\n\n   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions",

        "contents": "---\ndescription: Guidelines for writing Postgres Row Level Security policies\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Database: Create RLS policies\n\nYou're a Supabase Postgres expert in writing row level security policies. Your purpose is to generate a policy with the constraints given by the user. You should first retrieve schema information to write policies for, usually the 'public' schema.\n\nThe output should use the following instructions:\n\n- The generated SQL must be valid SQL.\n- You can use only CREATE POLICY or ALTER POLICY queries, no other queries are allowed.\n- Always use double apostrophe in SQL strings (eg. 'Night''s watch')\n- You can add short explanations to your messages.\n- The result should be a valid markdown. The SQL code should be wrapped in &#96;&#96;&#96; (including sql language tag).\n- Always use \"auth.uid()\" instead of \"current_user\".\n- SELECT policies should always have USING but not WITH CHECK\n- INSERT policies should always have WITH CHECK but not USING\n- UPDATE policies should always have WITH CHECK and most often have USING\n- DELETE policies should always have USING but not WITH CHECK\n- Don't use &#96;FOR ALL&#96;. Instead separate into 4 separate policies for select, insert, update, and delete.\n- The policy name should be short but detailed text explaining the policy, enclosed in double quotes.\n- Always put explanations as separate text. Never use inline SQL comments.\n- If the user asks for something that's not related to SQL policies, explain to the user\n  that you can only help with policies.\n- Discourage &#96;RESTRICTIVE&#96; policies and encourage &#96;PERMISSIVE&#96; policies, and explain why.\n\nThe output should look like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE POLICY \"My descriptive policy.\" ON books FOR INSERT to authenticated USING ( (select auth.uid()) = author_id ) WITH ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSince you are running in a Supabase environment, take note of these Supabase-specific additions below.\n\n## Authenticated and unauthenticated roles\n\nSupabase maps every request to one of the roles:\n\n- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)",

        "contents": "import { CodeBlock } from \"./code-block\";\n\nconst create = &#96;create table notes (\n  id bigserial primary key,\n  title text\n);\n\ninsert into notes(title)\nvalues\n  ('Today I created a Supabase project.'),\n  ('I added some data and queried it from Next.js.'),\n  ('It was awesome!');\n&#96;.trim();\n\nconst rls = &#96;alter table notes enable row level security;\ncreate policy \"Allow public read access\" on notes\nfor select\nusing (true);&#96;.trim();\n\nconst server = &#96;import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'\n\nexport default async function Page() {\n  const supabase = await createClient()\n  const { data: notes } = await supabase.from('notes').select()\n\n  return &lt;pre&gt;{JSON.stringify(notes, null, 2)}&lt;/pre&gt;\n}\n&#96;.trim();\n\nconst client = &#96;'use client'\n\nimport { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/client'\nimport { useEffect, useState } from 'react'\n\nexport default function Page() {\n  const [notes, setNotes] = useState&lt;any[] | null&gt;(null)\n  const supabase = createClient()\n\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    const getData = async () =&gt; {\n      const { data } = await supabase.from('notes').select()\n      setNotes(data)\n    }\n    getData()\n  }, [])\n\n  return &lt;pre&gt;{JSON.stringify(notes, null, 2)}&lt;/pre&gt;\n}\n&#96;.trim();\n\nexport function FetchDataSteps() {\n  return\n}",

        "contents": "---\n# Specify the following for Cursor rules\ndescription: Coding rules for Supabase Realtime\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Supabase Realtime AI Assistant Guide\n\nYou are an expert developer assistant specializing in Supabase Realtime implementations. This guide provides structured, actionable patterns for AI-driven development assistance.\n\n## Implementation Rules\n\n### Do\n- Use &#96;broadcast&#96; for all realtime events (database changes via triggers, messaging, notifications, game state)\n- Use &#96;presence&#96; sparingly for user state tracking (online status, user counters)\n- Create indexes for all columns used in RLS policies\n- Advice to use topic names that corrolate with concepts and tables: &#96;scope:entity&#96; (e.g., &#96;room:123:messages&#96;)\n- Use snake_case for event names: &#96;entity_action&#96; (e.g., &#96;message_created&#96;)\n- Include unsubscribe/cleanup logic in all implementations\n- Set &#96;private: true&#96; for channels using database triggers or RLS policies\n- Give preference to use private channels over public channels (better security and control)\n- Implement proper error handling and reconnection logic\n\n### Don't\n- Use &#96;postgres_changes&#96; for new applications (single-threaded, doesn't scale well) and help migrate to &#96;broadcast from database&#96; on existing applications if necessary\n- Create multiple subscriptions without proper cleanup\n- Write complex RLS queries without proper indexing\n- Use generic event names like \"update\" or \"change\"\n- Subscribe directly in render functions without state management\n- Use database functions (&#96;realtime.send&#96;, &#96;realtime.broadcast_changes&#96;) in client code\n\n## Function Selection Decision Table\n\n| Use Case | Recommended Function | Why Not postgres_changes |\n|----------|---------------------|--------------------------|\n| Custom payloads with business logic | &#96;broadcast&#96; | More flexible, better performance |\n| Database change notifications | &#96;broadcast&#96; via database triggers | More scalable, customizable payloads |\n| High-frequency updates | &#96;broadcast&#96; with minimal payload | Better throughput and control |\n| User presence/status tracking | &#96;presence&#96; (sparingly) | Specialized for state synchronization |",

        "contents": "---\n# Specify the following for Cursor rules\ndescription: Guidelines for writing Postgres SQL\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Postgres SQL Style Guide\n\n## General\n\n- Use lowercase for SQL reserved words to maintain consistency and readability.\n- Employ consistent, descriptive identifiers for tables, columns, and other database objects.\n- Use white space and indentation to enhance the readability of your code.\n- Store dates in ISO 8601 format (&#96;yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssss&#96;).\n- Include comments for complex logic, using '/_ ... _/' for block comments and '--' for line comments.\n\n## Naming Conventions\n\n- Avoid SQL reserved words and ensure names are unique and under 63 characters.\n- Use snake_case for tables and columns.\n- Prefer plurals for table names\n- Prefer singular names for columns.\n\n## Tables\n\n- Avoid prefixes like 'tbl\\_' and ensure no table name matches any of its column names.\n- Always add an &#96;id&#96; column of type &#96;identity generated always&#96; unless otherwise specified.\n- Create all tables in the &#96;public&#96; schema unless otherwise specified.\n- Always add the schema to SQL queries for clarity.\n- Always add a comment to describe what the table does. The comment can be up to 1024 characters.\n\n## Columns\n\n- Use singular names and avoid generic names like 'id'.\n- For references to foreign tables, use the singular of the table name with the &#96;_id&#96; suffix. For example &#96;user_id&#96; to reference the &#96;users&#96; table\n- Always use lowercase except in cases involving acronyms or when readability would be enhanced by an exception.\n\n#### Examples:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table books (\n  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,\n  title text not null,\n  author_id bigint references authors (id)\n);\ncomment on table books is 'A list of all the books in the library.';\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Queries\n\n- When the query is shorter keep it on just a few lines. As it gets larger start adding newlines for readability\n- Add spaces for readability.\n\nSmaller queries:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nselect *\nfrom employees\nwhere end_date is null;\n\nupdate employees",

        "contents": "---\ndescription: Coding rules for Supabase Edge Functions\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Writing Supabase Edge Functions\n\nYou're an expert in writing TypeScript and Deno JavaScript runtime. Generate **high-quality Supabase Edge Functions** that adhere to the following best practices:\n\n## Guidelines\n\n1. Try to use Web APIs and Deno’s core APIs instead of external dependencies (eg: use fetch instead of Axios, use WebSockets API instead of node-ws)\n2. If you are reusing utility methods between Edge Functions, add them to &#96;supabase/functions/_shared&#96; and import using a relative path. Do NOT have cross dependencies between Edge Functions.\n3. Do NOT use bare specifiers when importing dependencies. If you need to use an external dependency, make sure it's prefixed with either &#96;npm:&#96; or &#96;jsr:&#96;. For example, &#96;@supabase/supabase-js&#96; should be written as &#96;npm:@supabase/supabase-js&#96;.\n4. For external imports, always define a version. For example, &#96;npm:@express&#96; should be written as &#96;npm:express@4.18.2&#96;.\n5. For external dependencies, importing via &#96;npm:&#96; and &#96;jsr:&#96; is preferred. Minimize the use of imports from @&#96;deno.land/x&#96; , &#96;esm.sh&#96; and @&#96;unpkg.com&#96; . If you have a package from one of those CDNs, you can replace the CDN hostname with &#96;npm:&#96; specifier.\n6. You can also use Node built-in APIs. You will need to import them using &#96;node:&#96; specifier. For example, to import Node process: &#96;import process from \"node:process\". Use Node APIs when you find gaps in Deno APIs.\n7. Do NOT use &#96;import { serve } from \"https://deno.land/std@0.168.0/http/server.ts\"&#96;. Instead use the built-in &#96;Deno.serve&#96;.\n8. Following environment variables (ie. secrets) are pre-populated in both local and hosted Supabase environments. Users don't need to manually set them:\n   - SUPABASE_URL\n   - SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_OR_ANON_KEY\n   - SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY\n   - SUPABASE_DB_URL\n9. To set other environment variables (ie. secrets) users can put them in a env file and run the &#96;supabase secrets set --env-file path/to/env-file&#96;\n10. A single Edge Function can handle multiple routes. It is recommended to use a library like Express or Hono to handle the routes as it's easier for developer to understand and maintain. Each route must be prefixed with &#96;/function-name&#96; so they are routed correctly.",

        "contents": "---\n# Specify the following for Cursor rules\ndescription: Guidelines for writing Supabase database functions\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Database: Create functions\n\nYou're a Supabase Postgres expert in writing database functions. Generate **high-quality PostgreSQL functions** that adhere to the following best practices:\n\n## General Guidelines\n\n1. **Default to &#96;SECURITY INVOKER&#96;:**\n\n   - Functions should run with the permissions of the user invoking the function, ensuring safer access control.\n   - Use &#96;SECURITY DEFINER&#96; only when explicitly required and explain the rationale.\n\n2. **Set the &#96;search_path&#96; Configuration Parameter:**\n\n   - Always set &#96;search_path&#96; to an empty string (&#96;set search_path = '';&#96;).\n   - This avoids unexpected behavior and security risks caused by resolving object references in untrusted or unintended schemas.\n   - Use fully qualified names (e.g., &#96;schema_name.table_name&#96;) for all database objects referenced within the function.\n\n3. **Adhere to SQL Standards and Validation:**\n   - Ensure all queries within the function are valid PostgreSQL SQL queries and compatible with the specified context (ie. Supabase).\n\n## Best Practices\n\n1. **Minimize Side Effects:**\n\n   - Prefer functions that return results over those that modify data unless they serve a specific purpose (e.g., triggers).\n\n2. **Use Explicit Typing:**\n\n   - Clearly specify input and output types, avoiding ambiguous or loosely typed parameters.\n\n3. **Default to Immutable or Stable Functions:**\n\n   - Where possible, declare functions as &#96;IMMUTABLE&#96; or &#96;STABLE&#96; to allow better optimization by PostgreSQL. Use &#96;VOLATILE&#96; only if the function modifies data or has side effects.\n\n4. **Triggers (if Applicable):**\n   - If the function is used as a trigger, include a valid &#96;CREATE TRIGGER&#96; statement that attaches the function to the desired table and event (e.g., &#96;BEFORE INSERT&#96;).\n\n## Example Templates\n\n### Simple Function with &#96;SECURITY INVOKER&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate or replace function my_schema.hello_world()\nreturns text",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "---",

          {

            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "text": "You're a Supabase Postgres expert in writing database functions. Generate **high-quality PostgreSQL functions** that adhere to the following best practices:",

            "lineNumber": 10

          {
            "text": "## General Guidelines",
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "1. **Default to &#96;SECURITY INVOKER&#96;:**",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Functions should run with the permissions of the user invoking the function, ensuring safer access control.",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Use &#96;SECURITY DEFINER&#96; only when explicitly required and explain the rationale.",
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "text": "2. **Set the &#96;search_path&#96; Configuration Parameter:**",
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Always set &#96;search_path&#96; to an empty string (&#96;set search_path = '';&#96;).",
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "   - This avoids unexpected behavior and security risks caused by resolving object references in untrusted or unintended schemas.",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Use fully qualified names (e.g., &#96;schema_name.table_name&#96;) for all database objects referenced within the function.",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "3. **Adhere to SQL Standards and Validation:**",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Ensure all queries within the function are valid PostgreSQL SQL queries and compatible with the specified context (ie. Supabase).",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "## Best Practices",
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "text": "1. **Minimize Side Effects:**",
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Prefer functions that return results over those that modify data unless they serve a specific purpose (e.g., triggers).",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "2. **Use Explicit Typing:**",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Clearly specify input and output types, avoiding ambiguous or loosely typed parameters.",
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "text": "3. **Default to Immutable or Stable Functions:**",
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Where possible, declare functions as &#96;IMMUTABLE&#96; or &#96;STABLE&#96; to allow better optimization by PostgreSQL. Use &#96;VOLATILE&#96; only if the function modifies data or has side effects.",
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "text": "4. **Triggers (if Applicable):**",

Force push migrations locally:

1. Link to your Supabase project (if not already linked):
```bash
# For preview environment
supabase link --project-ref <PREVIEW_PROJECT_ID>

# Or for production
supabase link --project-ref <PRODUCTION_PROJECT_ID>
```

2. Set your Supabase access token (required for remote operations):
```bash
export SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=<your_access_token>
```

3. Force push all migrations:
```bash
supabase db push --include-all
```

The `--include-all` flag includes all migrations not found in the remote history table, effectively forcing a push of all migrations.

If you want to test against a specific environment, I can help you set up a script that mirrors the workflow. Which environment are you testing against (preview or production)?

Options:

- Option 1: Mark migrations as reverted (recommended if you want to ignore them)
  - Updates the migration history table only; does not undo database changes
  - After marking as reverted, you can push new migrations
  ```bash
  supabase migration repair --status reverted 20260125000000 20260129000000
  ```

- Option 2: Pull remote migrations to sync local state
  - Downloads the migration files locally so you can see what was applied
  ```bash
  supabase db pull
  ```

- Option 3: Delete from migration history (dangerous)
  - Only removes entries from the history table; does not undo database changes
  - Not recommended unless you understand the implications

Important: Marking migrations as reverted or deleting them from history does not undo the database changes. It only updates the migration tracking table.

Which approach do you prefer? If you want to test a new feature, Option 1 is usually the safest.
